name: Code prop types on, layout reflows across breakpoints
looks: A short component code snippet types on above an empty canvas, a prop value highlighted in the line. Below it a single narrow column of filled pills sits beside a width ruler; the ruler extends rightward, breakpoint pills light up as it passes them, and the column springs apart into four pills side by side.
build: The code types on with terminal-type-on, the changed prop value highlighted in the brand accent as it lands. The reflow uses responsive-breakpoint-scrub: the ruler's width tweens on the clock, breakpoint markers fade/scale in as it crosses them, and each pill's x/width interpolates from its stacked slot to its row slot in lockstep.
sound: A key tick under the code, then a rising tick per breakpoint crossed.
prompt: Type on a short piece of real configuration code with one prop highlighted, then prove what it does: show a layout sample reflow live as a width ruler extends past labelled breakpoints, a single stacked column springing apart into a row of elements exactly as the ruler crosses each marker.
